transcript.content: Hello, welcome. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. I'm... well, I'm here because, honestly, things have just gotten completely out of hand at my job. I work at a dry cleaner—I've been doing laundry and dry cleaning work for a long time—but lately, I just cannot seem to keep my work in order anymore. It's like my brain just stops working when I look at my counter. 

I mean, I'll have the customer tickets—you know, those little numbered tags, the pink and yellow ones—and the cash register receipts, and then these workshop notes my boss leaves me about, like, which garments need special spotting or delicate washing, and then the actual customer jobs, the piles of clothes themselves... and they all just end up piled together in this huge, messy mountain. I try to sort it out, I really do, but they just get mixed up, and I stand there staring at this massive pile and I just... I absolutely do not know what to handle first. I'll pick up a workshop note, then put it down to grab a receipt, and then I've lost the note under a pair of pants, and it's just so overwhelming. It's embarrassing, really, and I just don't understand why I can't just keep a simple workspace organized like I'm supposed to.
Have you been having persistent, unwanted thoughts or found yourself needing to perform certain actions repeatedly to feel less distressed?

Oh, no, it's not really like that. I don't have, you know, a specific bad thought stuck in my head that won't go away, or anything like that. It's actually kind of the opposite problem! My brain won't stick to just one thought long enough. It's more like I have fifty different thoughts all shouting at the same time, bouncing around like popcorn. 

But as for doing things over and over to feel less stressed... no, I don't do that. I mean, I know what you mean, like my neighbor, she has to check her front door lock exactly three times before she goes to bed or she can't sleep. I don't have anything like that. I'll check my pockets for my keys a lot, sure, but that's just because I'm always misplacing them and locking myself out of the house, not because I have some urge to do it to calm my nerves. It's just practical, really, since I lost them twice last month and had to call my husband at his job to come let me in, which he wasn't too thrilled about, let me tell you. 

But no, I don't have rituals or unwanted thoughts that I can't shake. My head is just full of regular, everyday clutter—like, Did I tag that wool coat? or I need to buy milk, or Where did I put my favorite pen?—and it all just hits me at the exact same time. Honestly, if I could just do one thing repeatedly and actually stick to it, I'd probably be in much better shape at the dry cleaners! So, no, nothing like what you're describing.
Outside of work, do you find it hard to stay organized or focused on tasks at home, like managing chores, keeping track of personal items, or following through on plans?

Oh, at home? Well, let me think about that. I guess... I mean, yes, but it's not like I don't try. I really do try. Take my kitchen, for instance. I'll decide, okay, today is the day I'm going to finally clean out the refrigerator, because, honestly, there are things in there from who knows when, and my husband is always complaining about the tupperware situation. So I'll start taking things out, right? I'll get the milk and the leftovers out on the counter, and then I'll notice that the counter is sticky. So I go to get the sponge, but the sponge smells awful, so I think, okay, I need to get a new sponge from the pantry. 

But when I open the pantry, I see that the canned goods are all jumbled up, and I can't find the sponges, but I do find that bag of dog treats I bought three weeks ago and completely forgot about. So then I think, oh, I should give Buster a treat! And I go find the dog, who is usually in the living room, and while I'm in there, I notice the mail piled up on the coffee table. And I think, oh no, I need to pay the electric bill, I meant to do that yesterday! So I sit down to sort the mail, and before I know it, two hours have gone by, I'm halfway through a magazine article about gardening, the mail is in three different piles on the floor, the dog has eaten half the bag of treats, and the refrigerator door is still wide open with the milk getting warm on the sticky counter. 

And my personal items? Oh, don't even get me started. Like I said about the keys earlier... it's not just keys. It's my glasses, my phone, my purse. I have this system where I'm supposed to put my purse on the little hook by the door the second I walk in, but somehow it ends up on the kitchen chair, or the bathroom counter, or once, I swear, I found it in the laundry basket under a pile of towels. I just put things down without thinking, and then they're gone. And plans? Well, I have a calendar on the fridge, a really nice one with pictures of lighthouses, but I forget to look at it. Or I'll write something down, like a dentist appointment, but I'll write it on a sticky note instead of the calendar, and then the sticky note falls off and gets swept under the fridge. So yes, I suppose you could say it's hard to stay organized at home, too. It just feels like I'm constantly spinning my wheels and never actually getting anywhere, you know? It's exhausting, it really is.

When you're trying to get things done, do you feel like your difficulties with staying focused and organized have been happening consistently for most of your life, or is this something that started more recently and seems tied to a specific stressor or low mood?

Oh, no, it's definitely not a new thing. Not at all. I mean, sometimes my husband will ask if maybe I'm just stressed about money or if it's, you know, my age catching up with me, but if I'm being completely honest with myself... and with you... it’s really been this way my whole entire life. I mean, going all the way back to when I was a little girl. 

Even in grade school, I remember my teachers were always, always telling my mother the exact same things. They’d pull her aside at those parent-teacher conferences—or write these long notes in cursive on the back of my report cards—and they would always tell her that I was a bright girl, which was sweet of them to say, but that I was just completely scattered. That was the word they always used. Scattered. 

I was always getting in trouble for talking out of turn, too. I just couldn't seem to hold a thought in! If something popped into my head during a spelling lesson, I’d just blurt it right out before I even realized my hand wasn't raised. And my desk... oh my goodness, it was a disaster area, just like my counter at the dry cleaners today. I was constantly losing my papers. I’d actually do the homework, I swear I did, but by the time I got to school, it was just gone. Crumpled at the bottom of my backpack or left on the kitchen table next to my cereal bowl. 

My mother used to get so frustrated with me, bless her heart, because the teachers said I constantly needed reminders just to finish my work. I’d start a worksheet, do the first three math problems, and then I’d be staring out the window watching a squirrel or peeling the paper off my crayon, completely forgetting I even had an assignment in front of me until the teacher tapped on my desk. So, no, it's not tied to feeling down lately or any new stress. It’s just... it’s just how my brain has always worked, ever since I was little, and I've just been dragging it along with me all these years.

Can you tell me if these issues with focus and organization also affect other areas of your life, like when you're out with friends, in social situations, or even when you're just trying to relax and read a book or watch TV?

Oh, it really does spill over into absolutely everything. You mentioned reading a book? I honestly can't tell you the last time I actually finished a book. I’ll read the exact same paragraph four or five times, and my eyes are moving over the words, but my brain is a million miles away, usually worrying about something else. 

Usually, I'm worrying about the shop, to be completely honest. Because it’s not just a messy counter there, it’s actually causing real problems that I just can't seem to get a handle on. We’ve been having late orders because I lose track of which garments came in when, or I'll put a rush tag on the wrong pile, and the billing... oh my goodness, the billing has gotten so confused lately. I’ll mix up the tickets or forget to enter a payment into the register because I got distracted by the phone ringing, and it’s just led to some really tense moments with the rest of the staff. They get annoyed having to fix my mistakes, which I completely understand, but it still hurts. And the customers... well, you know how people are about their clothes. If a suit isn't ready for a big meeting or a dress isn't pressed for a wedding, they get very upset, so there have been some very tense moments with the customers, too. It makes me dread going in sometimes.

And then socially... well, yes, it affects that too. Like at my church. I've gone to the same church for fifteen years, and I always loved being involved in the planning committees—the bake sales, the holiday bazaars, the spring picnic, all of that. But recently, I actually had to step back from leading some of the planning. I just couldn't keep the schedules straight, or I’d forget to call the vendors I said I was going to call, or I'd show up to a meeting having completely forgotten to bring the sign-up sheets. And... well, people were getting frustrated with me. I could see it. They were being polite, mostly, because it's church, but you can tell when someone is just fed up with you constantly dropping the ball. So I just stepped down. It broke my heart a little, it really did, but it was just too much pressure and I felt like I was letting everyone down. 

Even just trying to relax and watch TV with my husband is hard! He’ll put on a movie, a mystery or something, and twenty minutes in, I have to ask him who a character is or what they just said, because my mind drifted off to the church bake sale or the confused billing at the dry cleaners. He gets so exasperated with me, saying I don't pay attention. So, yes, it really feels like it interferes with just about everything, not just the chores at home. It’s everywhere, all the time.
